summary: SANS-Guard is an interactive web platform that detects early Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS) in astronauts using four quick, objective tests (visual acuity, facial swelling, star tracking, and line straightening). It provides a clear Green, Yellow, or Red triage alert to ensure timely medical intervention before vision damage occurs.
details:
The Problem During long-duration space missions, microgravity causes bodily fluids to shift upward toward the head, increasing pressure on the brain and eyes. This leads to Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), which causes blurred vision, facial swelling, eye-movement headaches, and visual distortion where straight lines appear curved. Without bulky clinical ophthalmic tools on board, astronauts need a fast, self-administered way to detect these subtle changes early. ​Our Solution: SANS-Guard We built an interactive, astronaut-friendly web dashboard featuring four real-time diagnostic assessments: ​Visual Acuity Test: Letters gradually shrink while the astronaut adjusts a slider and stops at the smallest legible size to track daily vision sharpness. ​Facial Edema Tracker: Uses the device camera with a calibrated face frame and slider so astronauts can compare and quantify facial swelling against their baseline. ​Headache & Eye-Tracking Test: A moving star travels across the screen (up, down, left, right); covering one eye at a time, the astronaut tracks it and compares pre- and post-test headache intensity. ​Line Straightness Calibration: Presents a curved line that the astronaut manually adjusts until it looks 100% straight—measuring hidden retinal distortion if they stop while the line is still curved. ​Impact & benefits: At the end of the session, SANS-Guard calculates an overall risk status: Green (healthy/stable), Yellow (minor changes requiring closer monitoring), or Red (high risk requiring immediate consultation with flight surgeons on Earth). By turning standard onboard cameras and screens into an objective diagnostic tool, SANS-Guard saves spacecraft payload mass, takes only minutes a day, and protects astronauts' eyesight before permanent damage develops.

So it has many benefits as Zero Extra Payload: Operates entirely on existing onboard screens and tablets, eliminating the need for bulky, specialized medical hardware in space.

also Objective & Quantifiable Tracking: Converts subjective symptoms into measurable daily baselines (tracking visual acuity, grid distortion, and fluid-shift changes over time) rather than relying on guesswork.

Programming Languages & Tools: ​HTML, CSS telwind, JavaScript,three.js,

and deploy by vercel ​Tools & Software: ​Google Gemini - Used for code debugging descriptions. ​Google Stitch - Used for initial UI layout concepts and design ideas. ​Figma - Used for manual UI/UX interface design and prototyping.

​Creativity & Innovation: Unlike traditional static medical checklists, SANS-Guard transforms complex neuro-ocular diagnostics into an engaging, gamified daily experience. By combining interactive visual calibrations—such as dynamic letter scaling, slider-based facial edema comparison, ocular star-tracking, and line-straightness alignment—with a space-themed dark-mode interface and a friendly astronaut-doctor mascot, we make self-monitoring intuitive, stress-free, and quantifiable for astronauts in microgravity.

​Key Factors Considered: Our team considered four key factors when designing SANS-Guard: spacecraft payload constraints (relying solely on existing onboard screens without bulky medical equipment), astronaut time and usability (creating a fast, intuitive dark-mode interface with simple slider controls), objective accuracy (replacing subjective checklists with measurable visual calibrations like line-straightness and dynamic letter scaling), and timely safety intervention (implementing an instant Green, Yellow, and Red triage alert system to flag when to contact flight surgeons on Earth).
